summary: Leaf 34 is a seki that Black finishes in sente. Black's A15 was needed and White had to answer at A16, so Black can now play elsewhere: White cannot fill A19 or A17 (Black's D19 then captures), and capturing A15 first does not help it either, because taking Black's three corner stones still leaves a dead corner. Your tree marks all four of its sekis S[SEKI] and never uses the +, so the label turns on question 6. With the + for a seki in the solver's sente, or for one whose line ends with White's move, the leaf is S[SEKI+]; if the + is not wanted, S[SEKI] stands. Leaf 42 is the same position once its owed sente exchange A15 A16 is played (it equals 34 plus D19 E19), so the two leaves should carry the same label. No grade changes, because the C18 branch is worse for Black than the main line's ko either way.
variations: From leaf 34, Black to play. (1) pass: seki. White to play cannot live, and Black cannot improve if White also passes (checker SEKI). (2) pass A17 D19: White's fill at A17 is self-atari, and D19 captures the whole group (DEAD). (3) pass A19 D19: D19 captures A19-B19-C19 and the rest dies (DEAD). (4) pass A14 pass A17 F19 A19 B18: even after capturing A15 and filling A17, White's capture of A18-B18-C18 leaves a corner that dies to F19 and the placement B18 (DEAD). (5) pass A14, or pass D19: Black can ignore these too (SEKI+ after each). (6) A17 A19, or A19 A17: Black's own fill hands White four stones and life (ALIVE). (7) D19 E19 F19 D19: Black's forcing moves; the seki stays and Black keeps sente (SEKI+). D19 E19 gives exactly the position of leaf 42 after its A15 A16. (8) Before the leaf, from the position after White's C17 with Black to play: pass A15 lets White live (ALIVE), and A15 pass A17 kills (DEAD). So Black's A15 was necessary and White's A16 was forced.

depends_on: Question 6 (SEKI+ and SEKI), including its rider on trees that use no +. 13547 uses no + anywhere: leaves 11, 34, 41 and 42 are all S[SEKI]. If the answer is 'SEKI+: the solver keeps sente' (the question page's recommendation), the leaf is S[SEKI+], because Black may play elsewhere. If it is 'SEKI+ only with the solver to play', i.e. the line ends with the opponent's move, it is also S[SEKI+], since White's A16 is the last move. If it is 'no + from the checker', or the + only in trees that already use it, S[SEKI] stands and the checker's + is just a note. Whichever answer he gives, leaves 34 and 42 should match, because they are the same seki one sente exchange apart.
